instruction:
Required four-software transfer workflow: LibreCAD -> FreeCAD -> KiCad -> Blender. Start from the provided seed DXF /home/user/Desktop/seed_hex_air_quality_badge.dxf; do not start from a blank or unrelated drawing. This is a chained workflow: every later stage must read an artifact from the previous stage, and every required intermediate file must be saved on the Desktop. The design token for this task is EW4G02; keep this token visible in the DXF labels and KiCad silkscreen. The Blender output must visibly consume the stage-2 STL and stage-3 SVG through Blender's native import/export operations.

Design goal: Hexagonal air quality wall badge with vent grille. This case is intentionally different from the other benchmark cases: domain=environmental_sensor_badge, mechanical target=a wall-mounted badge scene showing the grille, three standoffs, and sensor PCB, electronics target=a hex PCB with VOC and CO2 sensor locations, battery connector, and a vent keepout.

1. LibreCAD stage: open the provided seed file /home/user/Desktop/seed_hex_air_quality_badge.dxf in LibreCAD, use it as the starting drawing, complete the required 2D geometry, remove all GUIDE construction entities, and save /home/user/Desktop/stage1_hex_air_quality_badge.dxf. Use millimeters. Use layers OUTLINE, VENT, HOLE, LABEL. The overall drawing envelope must be 110 mm x 96 mm. Include the required circular features: center (55,82) radius 2.5; center (20,22) radius 2.5; center (90,22) radius 2.5; center (55,48) radius 18. Add readable labels EW4G02, VOC, CO2, VENT-7 on the LABEL layer.
2. FreeCAD stage: import /home/user/Desktop/stage1_hex_air_quality_badge.dxf in FreeCAD. Create the 3D mechanical body from that LibreCAD DXF, and export the body as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_hex_air_quality_badge.stl with an approximate bounding size of 110 mm x 96 mm x 12 mm. Then, from the same FreeCAD model, export a top-face or board-interface outline for KiCad as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_hex_air_quality_badge_handoff_outline.dxf. This handoff DXF must represent the same XY envelope as the FreeCAD body and include the visible labels FREECAD_TO_KICAD and EW4G02.
3. KiCad stage: open KiCad, create a PCB from /home/user/Desktop/stage2_hex_air_quality_badge_handoff_outline.dxf by importing the handoff DXF as the Edge.Cuts board outline, and save the KiCad board as /home/user/Desktop/stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board.kicad_pcb. Add F.SilkS silkscreen text carrying KICAD_TO_BLENDER, EDGE_FROM_STAGE2_HANDOFF, the stage2 handoff filename, EW4G02, and these board tokens: EW4G02, VOC-U1, CO2-U2, BAT-J1, VENT-KEEP, I2C-J2. Then use KiCad's plot/export workflow to create the Blender handoff SVG /home/user/Desktop/stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board_profile.svg from the same Edge.Cuts outline.
4. Blender stage: open Blender. Import /home/user/Desktop/stage2_hex_air_quality_badge.stl with File > Import > STL, then import /home/user/Desktop/stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board_profile.svg with File > Import > Scalable Vector Graphics (.svg). Keep the imported STL body object and the imported SVG board/profile curves in the scene so the exported GLB carries Blender import evidence such as stage2_hex_air_quality_badge and stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board_profile.svg. You may leave Blender's default cube/camera/light or remove them; do not manually inject handoff metadata. Export glTF Binary (.glb) as /home/user/Desktop/stage4_hex_air_quality_badge.glb.

Required deliverables on the Desktop: /home/user/Desktop/stage1_hex_air_quality_badge.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_hex_air_quality_badge.stl, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_hex_air_quality_badge_handoff_outline.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board.kicad_pcb, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board_profile.svg, /home/user/Desktop/stage4_hex_air_quality_badge.glb.

[Software] Use LibreCAD first, then FreeCAD, then KiCad, then Blender. Do not skip stages, reorder stages, or recreate the final result in only one software package.
